summary: Four experiments completed within the reported 0.0-minute milestone window, including one compute-bound experiment. Chronological causal-edge verified-memory stream was the sole and therefore longest compute-bound entry, reported at 0 minutes; the data gives no cause for its duration. No compute-task GPU-idle condition is recorded, and the snapshot does not establish accelerator efficiency or a runner-selection failure during execution.
bottlenecks_identified: Minute-rounded fallback timing reports all four entries at 0 minutes, preventing meaningful critical-path ranking or causal diagnosis.
The GPU report is not correlated with the compute task's execution window, so the snapshot cannot establish task-time accelerator efficiency.
Model-concurrency and runner-selection metadata are absent, so DualGPURunner eligibility or a missed dispatch cannot be determined.
improvements_suggested: Persist task-owned monotonic phase timing at sub-minute precision for every experiment.
Sample accelerator utilization during each compute task and attach the samples to that task's artifact.
Record loaded-model concurrency and the selected runner in launch receipts, choosing DualGPURunner only when concurrent model loading makes it applicable.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add task-owned phase clocks to expose setup, inference, validation, and artifact-write costs.
Join task-window GPU telemetry to each compute-bound experiment artifact.
Emit model-concurrency and runner-selection evidence in every compute launch receipt.
meta_reflection: The milestone completed too quickly at the reported precision to support a quantified speedup. Better task-correlated observability is the highest-leverage improvement because it would turn an ambiguous zero-minute reconstruction and point-in-time GPU snapshot into evidence that can guide scheduling changes.
